name: Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi
description: One of the Atamasthana sacred sites, this sacred fig tree was planted in 288 BC and is known as the oldest human-planted tree in the world with a known planting date.

name: Ruwanwelisaya
description: A magnificent white stupa built by King Dutugemunu in 140 BC, housing sacred relics of the Buddha. It is one of the highest monuments built in the ancient world.

name: Thuparamaya
description: The first Buddhist stupa constructed in Sri Lanka after the introduction of Buddhism, built during the reign of King Devanampiya Tissa (3rd century BC).

name: Lovamahapaya (Brazen Palace)
description: An ancient 9-story chapter house built by King Dutugemunu, featuring 1,600 stone pillars that once supported a massive bronze-roofed structure.

name: Abhayagiri Dagaba
description: A colossal ancient stupa and central monastic complex established in the 2nd century BC, celebrated for its advanced architectural engineering.

name: Jetavanaramaya
description: An enormous ancient brick stupa built by King Mahasena. At 122 meters, it was once the third-tallest structure in the ancient world.

name: Mirisavetiya Stupa
description: Built by King Dutugemunu after his victory, this historic stupa marks the spot where his scepter containing sacred Buddha relics could not be moved.

name: Lankarama
description: A stupa built in the 1st century BC by King Valagamba, originally housed inside a circular Vatadage with carved stone pillars.

name: Samadhi Buddha Statue
description: A famous 4th-century granite statue depicting the Buddha in the Dhyana Mudra meditation posture located within Mahamevnawa Park.

name: Isurumuniya Temple
description: An ancient rock-cut temple famed for its classical stone carvings, including the iconic 'Isurumuniya Lovers' and royal elephant reliefs around the lotus pond.

name: Kalu Diya Pokuna (Mihintale)
description: A tranquil sacred mountain complex regarded as the cradle of Sri Lankan Buddhism, where Arahat Mahinda met King Devanampiya Tissa in 247 BC.

name: Polonnaruwa Vatadage
description: A well-preserved circular relic house in the Dalada Maluwa (Quadrangle) featuring exquisite moonstones, guardstones, and four seated Buddha statues.

name: Gal Viharaya
description: A rock temple of the Buddha featuring four magnificent images carved into a single granite cliff face, including a massive 14-meter reclining Buddha.

name: Parakrama Samudra
description: A vast, 12th-century reservoir built by King Parakramabahu I, consisting of five interconnected lakes that reflect ancient Sri Lankan hydraulic mastery.

name: Statue of King Parakramabahu I
description: A majestic 12th-century stone carving near Potgul Viharaya depicting a king holding a manuscript scroll or a yoke, carved directly out of a boulder.

name: Royal Palace of King Parakramabahu
description: The imposing ruins of a 7-story palace complex that featured over a hundred rooms and thick brick walls reinforced by heavy timber framing.

name: Nissanka Latha Mandapaya
description: A unique open structure in the Quadrangle featuring stone pillars carved in the shape of curving lotus stalks, built by King Nissanka Malla.

name: Bahirawakanda Vihara Buddha Statue
description: A giant 88-foot white Buddha statue located on a hill overlooking Kandy city, offering expansive vistas of the lake and surrounding mountains.

name: Lankatilaka Vihara
description: A 14th-century temple built on a natural rock outcrop, combining Gampola era architecture with traditional stone brickwork and Kandyan wall paintings.

name: Gadaladeniya Vihara
description: An ancient 1344 AD South-Indian styled stone temple built atop a flat rock surface in Pilimathalawa by King Bhuvanekabahu IV.

name: Embekke Devalaya
description: Famous for its intricately carved wooden pillars in the main drum pavilion (Deva Santhakaya), showcasing 14th-century master craftsmanship.

name: Dambulla Cave Temple
description: A UNESCO World Heritage site and Sri Lanka's best-preserved rock cave temple complex, featuring 5 main sanctuaries filled with murals and 153 Buddha statues.

name: Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil
description: A major Hindu temple complex dedicated to Lord Murugan, renowned for its towering golden gopuram, intricate Dravidian architecture, and vibrant annual festivals.

name: Yapahuwa Rock Fortress
description: A dramatic 100-meter rock fortress that served as the capital of Sri Lanka in the late 13th century, featuring a magnificent, highly ornate stone staircase.

name: Muthumariamman Temple
description: A vibrant Hindu temple with a towering, colorfully adorned gopuram (gateway tower), dedicated to the goddess of rain and fertility.

name: Gonagala Viharaya
description: A picturesque cave temple situated near Kurunegala with a serene reclining Buddha statue and stunning views over the surrounding plains.

name: Sathmahal Prasada (Royal Palace Ruins)
description: The remains of a seven-storied palace believed to have been constructed by King Mahasena, offering insight into Anuradhapura's royal architecture.

name: Jethawanaramaya Dagoba
description: Once the tallest brick structure in the ancient world, this massive stupa is a dominant feature of the Anuradhapura skyline and a UNESCO site.

name: Mirisawetiya Stupa
description: A vast dagoba built by King Dutugemunu, located near the Thissa Wewa reservoir and surrounded by a serene meditation park.

name: Abhayagiri Dagoba and Monastery
description: One of the largest stupas in the world, surrounded by the ruins of a vast monastery complex that was once a center of Buddhist learning.

name: Jetavanaramaya Museum
description: Located near the Jethawanaramaya stupa, this museum houses artifacts unearthed from the ancient city, including pottery, sculptures, and ritual objects.

name: The Moonstone (Sandakada Pahana)
description: Semi-circular stone slabs found at the base of stairways in ancient Sri Lankan architecture, intricately carved with symbolic motifs like swans and elephants.

name: Jaffna Fort
description: A prominent star-shaped fort built by the Portuguese in 1618 and heavily fortified by the Dutch in 1680, overlooking the Jaffna lagoon.

name: Puttalam Dutch Fort
description: A historical colonial-era fortification constructed by the Dutch to guard trade routes along the western coast and control salt transport.

name: Trincomalee Harbour
description: One of the largest natural harbors in the world, holding immense historical, naval, and strategic maritime importance in Asia.

name: Shrine of Our Lady of Madhu (Madu Palliya)
description: A revered Roman Catholic shrine with a 400-year history, serving as a historic center of pilgrimage and spiritual unity in Sri Lanka.

name: Munneswaram Kovil
description: An ancient Hindu temple complex dedicated to Lord Shiva, revered as one of the Pancha Ishwarams with history tied to the Ramayana.

name: Koneswaram Kovil
description: A classical Hindu temple perched atop Swami Rock surrounded by the ocean, revered as an ancient Pancha Ishwaram dedicated to Shiva.

name: Avukana Buddha Statue
description: A magnificent 12-meter (39 ft) tall standing Buddha statue carved out of a granite rock face during the reign of King Dhatusena (5th century).

name: Wariyapola Sakman Buddha Statue
description: A notable walking Buddha statue located at Wariyapola Sri Sumangala Raja Maha Viharaya, honoring Ven. Wariyapola Sri Sumangala Thero.

name: Thirukonamalai Kaliamman Kovil
description: A vibrant Hindu temple located near the Koneswaram Kovil, dedicated to the goddess Kali Amman, famous for its colorful sculptures and spiritual atmosphere.

name: Thiruketheeswaram Kovil
description: One of Sri Lanka's five most sacred Hindu shrines dedicated to Shiva (Pancha Ishwarams), featuring ancient architecture and religious significance in the Vanni region.

name: Nagadeepa Purana Viharaya
description: An ancient Buddhist temple located on Nainativu Island, believed to mark the spot where the Buddha visited to settle a dispute between two Naga kings.

name: Nainativu Nagapooshani Amman Kovil
description: A prominent Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Parvati (Amman) situated on Nainativu Island, renowned for its stunning architecture and annual festivals.

name: Muthiyangana Temple
description: An ancient Buddhist temple located in Badulla town, believed to be the second-oldest dagoba site in Sri Lanka, with historical connections to the Buddha's visits.

name: Vavuniya Archaeological Museum
description: A regional museum showcasing artifacts recovered from archaeological sites in the Vavuniya and Mannar districts, including pottery, tools, and ancient sculptures.

name: Rathnaagiri Rajamaha Viharaya
description: An ancient Buddhist temple perched atop a rocky hill, featuring a serene atmosphere and panoramic views of the Kurunegala district. It houses significant Buddha statues and ancient cave paintings.

name: Wewurukannala Viharaya
description: A significant Buddhist temple located in Dickwella, renowned for its towering reclining Buddha statue, intricate wall murals, and the historic 'Wewurukannala Cave'.

name: Degaldoruwa Raja Maha Viharaya
description: A historic Buddhist temple located near Kandy, famous for its well-preserved 18th-century murals depicting Jataka tales and traditional Sri Lankan art.

name: Ritigala Archaeological Complex
description: A remote, ancient monastic complex hidden within a strict conservation forest, featuring ruins of stupas, meditation caves, and large stone platforms atop a forested mountain.

name: Gal Viharaya
description: An ancient Buddhist monastery renowned for its four magnificent Buddha statues carved out of solid granite, showcasing the pinnacle of Sri Lankan stone carving art.

name: Jambukola Viharaya
description: An ancient Buddhist temple believed to be the site where Theri Sanghamitta brought the Sacred Bodhi Sapling, historically significant for Buddhist history in Sri Lanka.

name: Jambukola Viharaya
description: An ancient Buddhist temple believed to be the site where Theri Sanghamitta brought the Sacred Bodhi Sapling, historically significant for Buddhist history in Sri Lanka.
